reading.title: A Day in the Invention Hall
reading.purpose: Follow two cousins as they try tools that see far, see small, and carry sound.
paras: On Saturday, Mei and her cousin Rafael spent the day in the Invention Hall of the science museum. In the first room, Mei bent over a brass telescope. She gasped, because the rings of Saturn, so far away, looked close enough to touch.

Next, Rafael slid a drop of pond water under a microscope. Something tiny wiggled across the glass. "That is a microbe," said the label, "a living thing too small to see without a tool." Rafael laughed. "There are hundreds of them in one drop!"

The sound gallery came after lunch. A guide handed Rafael a microphone, and his whisper boomed from the speakers. Then Mei tried a megaphone, a cone-shaped horn that sent her voice across the whole room. "Hello, everybody!" she shouted, and three visitors waved back.
In a quiet corner stood an old telegraph key. "People sent coded messages over wires with this," the guide said, "before anyone owned a telephone." Mei tapped her name in dots and dashes.

Near the exit, Rafael lifted a periscope to peek over a tall display case. Mei spun a kaleidoscope and watched colored bits make a new pattern with every turn. Then a symphony began to play, and the full orchestra seemed to fill the hall. On the bus home, the cousins agreed that the best tool was the one they had not tried yet.

choices: a thin glass plate that holds a drop of pond water
a tool that makes very small things look much bigger
a short label that explains what an exhibit shows
a living thing too small to see without a tool
qs.why: The label says a microbe is "a living thing too small to see without a tool."

qs.q: Which sentence shows what a telegraph was used for?
choices: "People sent coded messages over wires with this," the guide said, "before anyone owned a telephone."
Mei tapped her name in dots and dashes.
Something tiny wiggled across the glass.
Then Mei tried a megaphone, a cone-shaped horn that sent her voice across the whole room.
qs.why: Only this sentence tells the job of a telegraph: sending coded messages over wires.

ev.text: "People sent coded messages over wires with this," the guide said, "before anyone owned a telephone."

qs.q: Why did three visitors wave back at Mei?
choices: They wanted to borrow the megaphone so they could have a turn.
They heard her voice carry across the room and answered it.
They thought she was a museum guide who was giving a tour.
They were saying goodbye because the gallery was closing.
qs.why: Her voice was sent across the whole room by the megaphone, so the visitors heard her greeting and waved back.

qs.q: Which sentence tells what this story is mostly about?
choices: Two cousins get lost in a huge museum and must ask a guide for help home.
Two cousins learn how to play their instruments in a large orchestra together.
Two cousins try tools that help people see far, see small, and send sound.
Two cousins build a brand-new invention to donate to the science museum.
qs.why: Each paragraph shows the cousins using a different tool, and together the tools see far, see small, or carry sound.
